title: Add tolerant retry adapter + async pullstream polyglot shim to align SDK ergonomics
author: Maya Chen
description: This PR introduces a tolerant retry adapter and an async pullstream compatibility shim across Python, TypeScript, and Go SDKs to reduce friction around transient auth failures and to provide a stable, ergonomic async iterator for streaming responses across languages. Motivation: customer-facing incidents showed frequent transient token handshake failures and inconsistent stream ergonomics between SDKs which made cross-team integration tests brittle. This change: 1) Adds a lightweight "tolerant" retry adapter that treats short-lived 401/429 windows as retryable with a configurable credit window and jittered backoff presets. 2) Implements a small polyglot async pullstream shim that standardizes the semantics of pull-based streaming (peek/prefetch/pause/resume) and exposes a minimal, typed surface in each SDK. 3) Harmonizes default retry/backoff profiles used by the hosted client to avoid cross-language divergence. 4) Adds interop tests and examples demonstrating token swap + stream resume scenarios. The description below documents design decisions and checklist.
commits: feat(retry): tolerant adapter with credit window; feat(stream): async pullstream shim (py/ts/go); refactor(sdk): unify backoff presets; test: add crosslang interop tests and fixtures; ci: add pipeline matrix for cross-sdk smoke; docs: API examples and migration notes
review_comments: Liam O'Neill: Nice consolidation. Please clarify why tolerant adapter defaults to a 5s credit window instead of per-request tokens. Also add a short note about when this is unsafe (long-lived auth rotations).
Author(Maya Chen): Added explanation in docs and added 'unsafe_for_long_rotations' flag to the adapter. Kept default conservative (5s) after benching -- prevents extra retries for slow clients.
Priya Kapoor: Found a race in Go pullstream when cancel is called during prefetch; suggested chan close pattern and an additional unit test.
Author: Fixed race by switching to a context-aware prefetch worker and added the unit test the reviewer requested. PTAL.
Jonas Berg: CI flake in TypeScript tests (timing-sensitive). Recommend using fake timers in the spec to avoid flaky waits.
Author: Updated TS tests to use lolex fake timers; re-ran CI, all green.
ci_log_summary: Initial CI: failed (py flake8 + go vet); second run after fixes: pass across matrix (py 3.8/3.10, node 18/20, go 1.20/1.21).
release_notes:
- Introduce tolerant retry adapter (configurable credit window + jittered backoff) across SDKs
- Add async pullstream polyglot shim to standardize streaming ergonomics (peek/prefetch/pause/resume)
- Bump SDK packages: python -> 1.12.0, typescript -> 2.4.1, go -> v1.5.3
- Add cross-language integration tests and examples for token-swap + stream-resume
migration_notes: Clients relying on immediate 401 propagation: if you previously relied on instant auth failure surfacing, set tolerant_adapter.enabled=false or reduce credit_window_ms to 0. Default behavior preserves UX for most apps but smooths transient blips. See docs/sdk-migration/tolerant-retry.md for examples.
notes_for_reviewers: Key things to validate: 1) Backoff presets in internal/compat/retry_presets.go match the values in sdks/python and sdks/typescript. 2) No new goroutine leak in pullstream prefetch worker on cancel. 3) Python async iterator exposes 'peek' and 'resume' semantics consistent with TS/Go.
qa_steps: 1) Run cross-sdk matrix in ci/pipelines/cross-sdk-matrix.yml. 2) Exercise examples/multi-sdk/stream-resume/ to verify resume after token-swap. 3) Run long-running soak (10m) with simulated token rotation to ensure tolerant adapter does not mask real auth expiry unless configured.
related_issues: ENG-2401: transient auth handshake aborts in hosted infra
notes: This PR intentionally keeps the adapter implementation minimal (no persistent token cache or credential orchestration) — integration with the credential mediator will be done in a follow-up to keep review scope manageable.
